raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #41151.

HIP hands workgroups to the eight XCDs of an MI300-series GPU round-robin, and the Triton decode stage-1 kernels put the batch on the fastest grid axis, so with an even batch each request's workgroups stay on one XCD or a fixed subset of them. When the batch is uneven, from CUDA-graph padding rows (`seq_len=1`) or a mix of long and short requests, the XCDs that hold the long requests set the kernel time while the others idle.

On ROCm, the Triton backend is the default for Gemma 4, MiniMax-M3, Olmo 3 and EXAONE, and for MLA models whose heads per rank are not 16 or 128, such as Kimi-K2 at TP 8.

## Modifications

- `get_num_kv_splits_triton` also writes a one-element `uneven_batch` flag: 1 when the shortest decode sequence is still shorter than the longest after the existing near-uniform rule.
- On HIP, for an even batch, the stage-1 kernels read the flag and, when it is set, rotate the request index across the grid: by head and split in the per-head kernel, by split only in the grouped (GQA/MLA) kernel, so the head tiles of one request and split still share the KV they read. Balanced batches, odd batches and CUDA run as before.
- `TritonAttnBackend` passes the flag through, with a static buffer for CUDA graphs.

Outputs are bitwise identical with and without the rotation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End to end on 1x MI325X (TP 1), main at `d8f85223` vs this PR, `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random-ids --seed 1`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.8` (the 26B-A4B runs also set `--context-length 135168`). Output tok/s, two runs each; "ragged" draws input and output lengths from 5–100% of the stated maximum.

| model | case | main | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemma-4-31B-it | 5 × (16K in, 1K out), padded into the bs-8 graph | 174.2, 173.4 | 178.7, 178.4 | +3% |
| gemma-4-31B-it | 4 × (16K in, 1K out) | 132.6, 132.1 | 132.4, 131.1 | 0% |
| gemma-4-31B-it | 8 × (16K in, 1K out) | 239.1, 238.8 | 238.7, 238.6 | 0% |
| gemma-4-31B-it | 64 × ragged (16K in, 1K out), conc 16 | 213.1, 213.2 | 223.3, 223.4 | +5% |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | 5 × (32K in, 1K out), padded into the bs-8 graph | 317.6, 309.9 | 322.7, 313.9 | +1% |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | 4 × (32K in, 1K out) | 224.1, 197.0 | 223.4, 194.2 | −1% |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | 8 × (32K in, 1K out) | 480.6, 444.8 | 477.6, 447.5 | 0% |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | 64 × ragged (32K in, 1K out), conc 16 | 370.4, 397.1 | 393.5, 419.0 | +6% |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | 192 × ragged (4K in, 512 out), conc 32 | 1338.1, 1347.3 | 1364.6, 1373.6 | +2% |

With `--context-length 135168 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1` and 32K inputs, gemma-4-31B-it decodes five requests padded into the bs-8 graph at 179 tok/s instead of 145 (three runs; +11–18% output tok/s over the whole run), and 64 ragged 32K requests at conc 16 gain 4.5%.

Kernel microbench: `decode_attention_fwd` at 32K context in a CUDA graph of 20 calls, best of 3 interleaved runs, KV splits sized as `TritonAttnBackend` does; time with the rotation / without. Sliding-window layers see at most 1024 tokens.

| layer (q heads / kv heads, head dim) | 5 → 8 padded | 20 → 24 padded | 1 × 32K + 7 × 1K | 32 random lengths | 8 uniform |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemma-4-31B global (32 / 4, 512) | 0.98 | 0.90 | 0.51 | 0.94 | 1.00 |
| gemma-4-31B sliding (32 / 16, 256) | 0.80 | 0.91 | 1.01 | 1.01 | 1.01 |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B global (16 / 2, 512) | 0.99 | 1.00 | 0.99 | 0.66 | 1.00 |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B sliding (16 / 8, 256) | 0.83 | 0.91 | 1.02 | 1.01 | 1.01 |
| MiniMax-M3 at TP 8 (8 / 1, 128) | 1.00 | 0.99 | 0.85 | 0.97 | 1.00 |
| Kimi-K2 MLA at TP 8 (8 heads, 576 / 512) | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.95 | 1.00 |

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K through the chat template (`sgl-eval run gsm8k`, 1319 questions, greedy), main / this PR: gemma-4-31B-it 0.970 / 0.970, gemma-4-26B-A4B-it 0.968 / 0.968.

## Checklist

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body: Thanks! @BBuf Rebased onto main and added `test_decode_attention_uneven_batch_graph_replay` to `test_triton_attention_kernels.py`, which runs in the AMD stage-b suite. It captures one decode graph and replays it over uniform, padded (`seq_len=1` rows) and ragged batches, refreshing the metadata through `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata` before each replay. Each replay has to see its own `uneven_batch` flag in the captured buffer and match an eager run without the rotation, for both the per-head and the grouped kernel. It passes on AMD GPUs, and it fails if the replay stops passing the flag buffer, if the flag gets stuck at 1, or if the rotation stops being a permutation.

@@ -45,6 +45,15 @@
 
 _MIN_BLOCK_KV = 32
 
+
+def _rotate_batch(batch: int, uneven_batch: Optional[torch.Tensor]) -> bool:
+    # HIP hands workgroups to XCDs round-robin. With batch as the fastest grid axis,
+    # an even batch keeps each request on a subset of XCDs, so a long request or
+    # CUDA-graph padding rows leave the other XCDs idle. A balanced batch is already
+    # spread evenly, so the kernels only rotate while uneven_batch holds 1.
+    return _is_hip and batch % 2 == 0 and uneven_batch is not None
+
+
 # heads per stage-1 tile, shared so the budget's head_tiles cannot drift from the launch
 _GROUPED_BLOCK_H = 16
 
@@ -264,12 +273,18 @@ def _fwd_kernel_stage1(
     aux0_stride_t=0,
     aux0_stride_h=0,
     aux0_len=0,
+    uneven_batch=None,
+    ROTATE_BATCH: tl.constexpr = False,
 ):
-    # int64 to avoid overflow of flat offsets into Mid_O when
-    # batch * num_head * max_kv_splits * head_dim exceeds 2**31.
-    cur_batch = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    cur_batch = tl.program_id(0)
     cur_head = tl.program_id(1)
     split_kv_id = tl.program_id(2)
+    if ROTATE_BATCH:
+        if tl.load(uneven_batch) != 0:
+            cur_batch = (cur_batch + cur_head + split_kv_id) % tl.num_programs(0)
+    # int64 to avoid overflow of flat offsets into Mid_O when
+    # batch * num_head * max_kv_splits * head_dim exceeds 2**31.
+    cur_batch = cur_batch.to(tl.int64)
 
     cur_kv_head = cur_head // kv_group_num
 
@@ -428,6 +443,7 @@ def _decode_att_m_fwd(

+    def test_decode_attention_uneven_batch_graph_replay(self):
+        """One captured decode graph replayed over uniform, padded and ragged batches.
+
+        TritonAttnBackend refreshes num_kv_splits and the uneven_batch flag in place
+        before each replay, and the captured stage-1 kernels read the flag at run time,
+        so every replay must see its own flag and match an eager run without rotation.
+        """
+        device = get_device()
+        dtype = torch.bfloat16
+        bs, pool, D, max_kv_splits = 8, 8192, 128, 8
+        rounds = [
+            ([600] * bs, 0),
+            ([600, 610, 620, 630, 640, 1, 1, 1], 1),  # CUDA-graph padding rows
+            ([600] * bs, 0),
+            ([1000] + [64] * (bs - 1), 1),
+            ([700] * bs, 0),
+        ]
+        for H_Q, H_KV in ((8, 8), (16, 2)):
+            backend = TritonAttnBackend.__new__(TritonAttnBackend)
+            backend.num_head, backend.num_kv_head = H_Q, H_KV
+            backend.max_kv_splits = max_kv_splits
+            backend.device_core_count = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(
+                device
+            ).multi_processor_count
+            backend.static_kv_splits = False
+            backend.enable_deterministic = False
+            backend.split_tile_size = None
+            backend.cuda_graph_num_kv_splits = torch.zeros(
+                bs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+            )
+            backend.cuda_graph_uneven_batch = torch.zeros(
+                1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+            )
+            backend._update_decode_kv_buffers = lambda plan, n, lens, req: (
+                None,
+                None,
+                None,
+                lens,
+            )
+
+            seq_lens = torch.zeros(bs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+            kv_indptr = torch.zeros(bs + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+            kv_indices = torch.zeros(pool, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+            q = torch.randn(bs, H_Q, D, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+            k_buffer = torch.randn(pool, H_KV, D, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+            v_buffer = torch.randn(pool, H_KV, D, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+            o = torch.empty(bs, H_Q, D, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+            attn_logits = torch.empty(
+                bs, H_Q, max_kv_splits, D, dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+            )
+            attn_lse = torch.empty(
+                bs, H_Q, max_kv_splits, dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+            )
+
+            def update(lens):
+                seq_lens.copy_(torch.tensor(lens, dtype=torch.int32))
+                kv_indptr[1:] = torch.cumsum(seq_lens, 0)
+                kv_indices[: sum(lens)] = torch.randperm(pool, device=device)[
+                    : sum(lens)

+                backend._apply_cuda_graph_metadata(
+                    None, bs, None, seq_lens, ForwardMode.DECODE, None
+                )
+
+            def decode(out, uneven_batch):

+                    k_buffer,
+                    v_buffer,
+                    out,
+                    kv_indptr,
+                    kv_indices,
+                    attn_logits,
+                    attn_lse,
+                    backend.cuda_graph_num_kv_splits,
+                    max_kv_splits,
+                    D**-0.5,
+                    1.0,
+                    1.0,
+                    enable_lean=False,
+                    uneven_batch=uneven_batch,
+                )
+
+            update(rounds[1][0])
+            decode(o, backend.cuda_graph_uneven_batch)
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()

+            flag_ptr = backend.cuda_graph_uneven_batch.data_ptr()

+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(backend.cuda_graph_uneven_batch.item(), uneven)
+                    self.assertTrue(torch.equal(o, ref))

issue_comments.body: Thanks! @BBuf Rebased onto main and added `test_decode_attention_uneven_batch_graph_replay` to `test_triton_attention_kernels.py`, which runs in the AMD stage-b suite. It captures one decode graph and replays it over uniform, padded (`seq_len=1` rows) and ragged batches, refreshing the metadata through `_apply_cuda_graph_metadata` before each replay. Each replay has to see its own `uneven_batch` flag in the captured buffer and match an eager run without the rotation, for both the per-head and the grouped kernel. It passes on AMD GPUs, and it fails if the replay stops passing the flag buffer, if the flag gets stuck at 1, or if the rotation stops being a permutation.
